newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: LME aluminium seen firmer on TOCOM, U.S. premiums.
newsitem.headline: LME aluminium seen firmer on TOCOM, U.S. premiums.

text.p: Three-month aluminium is expected to firm on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Thursday tracking gains on the new Tokyo aluminium futures contract and in anticipation of brisk demand helped by softening U.S. premiums.

"Three-month aluminium is expected to test recent psychological resistance at $1,600 a tonne today on the London Metal Exchange due to Tokyo aluminium's firmer tone," a trader with Tong Yang Futures said.
TOCOM's benchmark February aluminium contract closed 2.4 yen a kg higher at 209.0 yen on Thursday.

Another futures trader said softening U.S. aluminium premiums could help boost Asian physical demand, although this would take some time to affect the Asian market. U.S. premiums for nearby delivery of Western grade metal have slipped to between 5.25 to 5.50 cents per pound over LME cash, down from 6.0 cents and above last month when they reached a peak of about 7.00 cents.

Aluminium premiums, C&F Hong Kong, remained high, regional traders said citing levels around $130 a tonne, while premiums in Shanghai were quoted at $150 a tonne, a Singapore trader said, adding they could firm further.
"Producers are holding inventory and they want to sell at a real premium," he said.
"I can't see huge volumes changing hands at these levels, and with U.S. premiums softening you might start to see them coming off," he said.
High regional premiums were more of an anticipation of the effect of higher U.S. interest rates and short-term market mentality, said another trading source.
"There's a regional tighteness, yes, but demand is exceptionally good, so these premiums are needed to make it cost effective to draw the metal out of warehouses," he said.
"There's plenty of metal around, but the demand is on the other side of the world," he said.
The other trader pegged resistance for LME three-month aluminium at between $1,625-$1,630.

LME broker Brandeis said in its daily report that Wednesday's close of three-month aluminium above the 100-day Moving Average at $1,590 a tonne is another bullish factor but prices still need to breach resistance at $1,600 to move higher.
The 30-day Moving Average for three-month copper is also expected to act like a magnet to get copper back to $2,355 a tonne, a trader said.
Dealers said Chinese trading companies were buying small lots of copper to transship to smelters in the country's interior, and this was believed to be supporting prices.
With LME values buoyant, and the Shanghai Metal Exchange cash price bouncing around 23,000 yuan ($2,771) per tonne, arbitrage opportunities could be contributing to the Chinese import activity.
But one trader said although prices had picked up well on Wednesday from lows of around $2,264 a tonne, copper prices could struggle to move much higher due to the lack of fresh fundamental factors.
Technically, three-month zinc is seen being sound after filling the gap between $1,254 and $1,262 amid positive signs of recovery from a previously overbought situation.
The 14-day relative strength index (RSI) for three-month zinc was standing at 50.66 percent, compared to 67.59 percent a week ago.
The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
-- Jae Hur, Seoul Newsroom (822) 727 5651
